description: Cadence BioSystems was created to tackle a practical problem in deep-space missions: how a crew manages medical issues when Houston is up to 20 minutes away by radio. Instead of relying on live ground support, we are building CADENCE, an onboard health console designed to help astronauts without medical degrees track physiological trends, spot early warning signs across NASA's five spaceflight hazards, and walk through guided ultrasound and countermeasure checks independently.
summary:
CADENCE (Crew Autonomous Diagnostics & Expedition Care Engine) is an Earth-independent onboard health monitoring and clinical decision-support console engineered for long-duration spaceflight.

As crews venture beyond Low Earth Orbit toward the Moon and Mars, one-way communication delays of up to 18 minutes and 40 seconds, a 37-minute round-trip, renders real-time Mission Control flight surgeon guidance impossible during acute medical events. CADENCE bridges this autonomy gap by automatically activating Autonomous Onboard Triage whenever Earth latency exceeds five minutes. Grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) risks and flight-proven instrumentation including Tempus Pro vitals, CSA CANS neutron dosimetry, ARCHeR circadian actigraphy, Zero-T2 exercise protocols, and Philips L12-4 / Ultrasound-2 imaging. The console fuses multi-day physiological trend thresholds with an interactive anatomical digital twin, guided B-mode and Color Doppler ultrasound simulations, and structured countermeasure compliance tracking.

By distinguishing expected microgravity adaptation from actionable clinical drift such as Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), jugular venous stasis, solar radiation storms, pre-EVA hypoxia, and Martian gravity-transition orthostatic drops, CADENCE empowers non-physician crews to diagnose and stabilize health risks autonomously while offering immediate dual-use value for rural telemedicine and aging care on Earth.
details:
What Is CADENCE

CADENCE is a self-contained, Earth-independent clinical decision-support and physiological monitoring console engineered for human deep-space exploration. Designed specifically for missions extending beyond Low Earth Orbit, such as Lunar Gateway, Mars Transit, and Mars surface operations. CADENCE equips non-physician astronauts with real-time diagnostic synthesis, guided ultrasound imaging, multi-day drift detection, and structured countermeasure management when communication delays prevent live guidance from Mission Control.

What It Does & How It Works

CADENCE operates as a unified, aviation-grade flight-surgeon console organized around five core operational capabilities:

1. Latency Aware Mission Environments & Autonomous Mode

Operators can switch between four authentic mission environments: ISS LEO (0.5s one-way delay, Day 084 / 180), Lunar Gateway (2.6s delay, Day 014 / 030), Mars Transit (18m 40s delay, Day 142 / 540), and Mars Jezero Surface (14m 10s delay, Sol 001 / 500, 0.38g partial gravity).

Whenever one-way Earth signal latency exceeds 5 minutes (such as during Mars Transit or Jezero surface operations, where round-trip communication takes 28 to 37+ minutes), CADENCE automatically activates Autonomous Onboard Triage, shifting from ground-supported monitoring to independent onboard clinical decision-making.

2. Interactive 5-System Anatomical Digital Twin & NASA 5-Hazards Matrix

A central anatomical crew body map displays color-coded physiological status rings (Nominal, Drift Detected, Action Required) across Neuro-Ocular, Behavioral, Cardiovascular / Haemostasis, Respiratory / Immune, and Musculoskeletal / Sensorimotor systems.

Selecting any organ system filters diagnostics to that system while updating a live NASA 5-Hazards Matrix tracking Altered Gravity Fields, Space Radiation, Distance from Earth, Isolation & Circadian Sleep, and Hostile/Closed Environments.

3. Flight-Proven Telemetry & Dual-Trace 14-Day Trend Analytics

CADENCE benchmarks live crew metrics against individualized terrestrial baselines using real ISS and Artemis biomedical payloads: Tempus Pro vitals (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, core temperature, blood glucose), CSA CANS neutron radiation dosimetry (mSv/day), ARCHeR wrist actigraphy sleep tracking, and ECLSS cabin CO2 partial pressure.

Pure-SVG 14-day telemetry trend charts plot cumulative physiological drift against green Earth baseline reference lines, including a dual-trace HR / SysBP chart that visualizes the inverse compensatory relationship between heart rate (bpm) and systolic blood pressure (mmHg) during planetary gravity transitions.

4. Guided OCT / Ultrasound-2 Simulator (Philips L12-4 Linear Array)

An interactive diagnostic ultrasound module guides astronauts through two critical spaceflight scans:

  • Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter (ONS / SANS): Displays the vitreous globe, optic nerve sheath walls, and the clinical 3 mm posterior caliper landmark (4.8 mm nominal vs. 6.3 mm during cephalic fluid shift), complete with a Probe Alignment / Gel Coupling simulation that introduces realistic acoustic speckle noise and caliper jitter if probe contact drops below 70%
  • Internal Jugular Vein (IJV Doppler): Models longitudinal B-mode vessel walls alongside real-time Color Doppler blood-flow particles, contrasting healthy rhythmic wall compliance and blue antegrade drainage against engorged vessel walls and red retrograde/stasis eddies caused by microgravity venous congestion.
5. Interactive Scenario Suite, Offline Manual Check-In & Flight Discipline Tracker

Five end-to-end clinical presets demonstrate CADENCE across acute and gradual mission events: Nominal Baseline, SANS Fluid Shift, Solar Particle Event (CANS), EVA Prep: Hypoxia / DCS, and Gravity Transition.

An offline Manual Check-In tab allows astronauts to log symptoms and vitals directly into an onboard clinical rule engine, dynamically recalculating organ statuses and resolution states without external connectivity.

The Countermeasure Compliance & Readiness panel tracks daily preventive protocols (Thigh Cuffs, B-Complex Regimen, Zero-T2 Resistive Protocol, ARCHeR Circadian Hygiene, and Veggie Habitat Module) linked directly to flight clearance (GO FOR EVA, MONITOR, or EVA HOLD) and consecutive compliant sols.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Eliminating Communication-Delay Risk: By synthesizing multi-sensor telemetry and ultrasound landmarks onboard, CADENCE ensures crews on multi-year Mars expeditions can detect, verify, and stabilize life, or mission-threatening conditions without waiting nearly 40 minutes for a response from Earth.

Preventing Alarm Fatigue: Almost every astronaut experiences mild baseline fluid shifts upon entering microgravity. CADENCE distinguishes expected microgravity adaptation from actionable clinical drift (for example, silently tracking sub-clinical optic nerve sheath widening on the 14-day trend chart until it crosses the 5.8 mm threshold to 6.3 mm alongside sleep debt and missed thigh cuffs).

Terrestrial Dual-Use Healthcare Impact: Spaceflight accelerates human aging physiology, inducing bone density loss, muscle atrophy, vestibular balance deficits, cardiovascular deconditioning, and insulin resistance up to 10 times faster than on Earth. CADENCE's offline clinical decision support, guided non-expert ultrasound cues, and structured preventive compliance tracking translate directly to remote and rural telemedicine, polar/maritime expeditions, disaster response, and home care.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

Languages & Core Web Standards: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 2D Canvas API (for real-time B-mode acoustic speckle rendering, anatomical landmarks, and Color Doppler blood-flow particle physics), and inline Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) for interactive anatomical body mapping, circular readiness gauges, and dual-trace 14-day trend charts.

UI & Styling Architecture: Tailwind CSS utility framework paired with a custom dark-mode interface, 1px borders, high-contrast status badges (Emerald, Amber, Crimson), and monospace tabular typography (JetBrains Mono / Inter)

Domain & Scientific Grounding: Built directly around NASA Human Research Program (HRP) risk frameworks and flight-validated hardware specifications, including CSA CANS (Canadian Space Agency neutron dosimetry), ARCHeR (wrist actigraphy circadian monitoring), Tempus Pro (crew medical telemetry), Zero-T2 (resistive exercise), and Philips L12-4 / Ultrasound-2 imaging protocols.

Deployment & Hosting: Engineered as a zero-dependency, offline-first single-file web application (index.html) requiring zero external servers or cloud APIs, ensuring 100% reliability inside a deep-space habitat. Deployed publicly via Google Sites.

What Makes CADENCE Creative

Operational Flight Discipline: CADENCE models authentic astronaut operational discipline, linking real preventive countermeasures (such as Thigh Cuffs and B-Complex vitamins) to physiological root causes and live EVA flight clearance.

Chronological Mission Storytelling: The five scenarios form a cohesive expedition, from healthy cruise (Nominal Baseline), to mid-transit microgravity fluid drift (SANS Fluid Shift), deep-space radiation storms (Solar Particle Event), orbital spacewalk preparation (EVA Prep: Hypoxia / DCS), and landing on Mars in 0.38g (Gravity Transition).

Interactive Physics-Driven Ultrasound Simulation: Instead of static placeholder images, CADENCE simulates acoustic speckle noise, probe-alignment coupling jitter, and hemodynamic Doppler particle flow, showing both healthy antegrade jugular drainage and microgravity venous stasis in real time.

Key Factors Considered During Development

Zero-Network / Offline Resilience: Deep-space software cannot depend on cloud databases or external APIs; every calculation, SVG chart, and ultrasound simulation runs 100% locally in-browser.

Cognitive Load Under Stress: During an emergency, such as a solar radiation spike or hypoxia alert, astronauts face high cognitive stress. CADENCE prioritizes clear visual hierarchy, high-contrast status indicators, plain-language clinical explanations, and step-by-step action checklists.

Clinical & Aerospace Fidelity: Every physiological threshold (such as 6.3 mm Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter at 3 mm posterior depth, 96/62 mmHg orthostatic hypotension upon 0.38g Mars touchdown, and 18m 40s Mars transit latency) and mission timeline (180-day ISS increments, 30-day Lunar Gateway stays, 540-day Mars transit, and 500-Sol Martian surface stays) was calibrated against real NASA and CSA space medicine research.

Other Considerations and Future Scalability

While the current CADENCE prototype operates as a self-contained, zero-backend flight console ready for crew training and mission simulation, future development is structured into three phases:

Direct Wearable & Medical Hardware Ingestion: Integrating Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and USB telemetry streams from flight-certified wrist actigraphy monitors (such as ARCHeR), wireless pulse oximeters, and point-of-care ultrasound probes to replace simulated sensor feeds with live biometric data.

Store-and-Forward Flight Surgeon Downlink: Adding compressed, bandwidth-aware telemetry packet export (JSON / HL7 FHIR) so autonomous onboard triage logs, ultrasound snapshots, and countermeasure adherence records automatically synchronize with Mission Control whenever deep-space communication windows open.

Personalized Onboard Drift Forecasting: Incorporating lightweight, offline machine-learning models trained on individualized baseline trajectories to predict multi-system physiological drift (such as linking cumulative sleep debt and elevated cabin CO2 to early SANS progression) before clinical thresholds are crossed.
